subject: science
passage: Japanese macaques, which live farther north than any other nonhuman ______ have adapted to winters with deep snow. In Jigokudani, a valley in the mountains of central Japan, one troop is famous for soaking in natural hot springs, a habit that researchers first recorded in the 1960s and that the monkeys appear to have passed down through generations.
stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?

explanation.why: "Which live farther north than any other nonhuman primate" is extra information about the macaques. It opens with a comma after "macaques," so it must close with a comma too, before the verb "have adapted."
explanation.A: Correct. The closing comma matches the opening comma after "macaques" and completes the pair around the extra information.
explanation.B: Incorrect. Without a closing comma, the extra information is never set off and runs straight into the verb "have adapted."
explanation.C: Incorrect. A semicolon can't separate the subject "Japanese macaques" from its verb "have adapted."
explanation.D: Incorrect. Once the comma closes the extra information, "and have adapted" is left with nothing to join to; the subject "Japanese macaques" needs "have adapted" as its own verb, not as a second item after "and."
